A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same DR-IRL paper. Text and visual inspection support matching the methods, equations, tables, figures and appendices despite renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v4 reports original safety and helpfulness evaluations, ablations, jailbreak tests and reward-model comparisons in Section 4 and the supplementary material.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendix F, including benchmark scores, ablations and computational comparisons.

M1.justification: The category-specific IRL reward models, hardness coefficients and scaled GRPO updates remain unchanged. Section 3 and Algorithms 1–3 describe the same procedure; the redrawn pipeline does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: The training sources, seven harm categories, safety/helpfulness benchmarks and jailbreak scenarios are retained. Applications mentioned in the new broader-impacts discussion are not additional evaluated domains.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparators, including STAIR, GRPO and IRL. The jailbreak, OpenAI/Anthropic reward-model, additive-weighting and PPO/DPO comparisons also retain their original comparator membership after relocation.

E3.justification: The reported model configurations, training budgets, metrics and evaluation procedures are unchanged, including the 5% validation holdout and weight-selection procedure for the additive baseline. Newly stated data checking and filtering provide additional disclosure without establishing a revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same hardness, reward-model specialization/size, CoD, jailbreak and cross-optimizer analyses. Moving tables and removing a duplicate display do not change these analyses. The new manual-check statement reports no additional assessment outcomes.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same statements about initialization/data-shuffling seeds and smaller variance across seeds. No repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty-reporting procedures are added.

E6.justification: All matched result tables have identical numerical contents, and the empirical figure images are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains DR-IRL StrongReject scores of 0.9361 for Llama and 0.8798 for Qwen. The removed duplicate product-versus-sum table remains represented by Table 3.

T1.justification: The ML-IRL/minimax formulation, hardness definitions, optimization objectives and supplementary gradient and closed-form policy equations are retained. Equations 1–17 contain no substantive mathematical revision, and no theorem, assumption or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and core conclusion retain the claims of balanced demonstration-based IRL, difficulty-scaled GRPO and improved safety while preserving usefulness. The added discussion does not redefine the central scientific contributions.

C2.justification: v6 adds explicit limitations concerning synthetic data missing cultural cues or rare adversarial patterns and the cost of scaling category-specific reward models. It also discusses hidden biases from automated reward shaping and potential misuse. These qualify the retained efficacy interpretations.

D1.justification: Beyond v4's existing training details and generic repository mentions, v6 documents manual CoD checking, automatic/manual filtering and release conditions: research-only licensing, a data-use agreement, controlled API access and restricted model weights. These are additional disclosures; the technical training recipe remains unchanged, and no concrete repository or API access link is supplied.

R1.justification: v6 adds citations including Hsu et al. (2024), Jiang et al. (2025), Wu et al. (2025) and recent attack/defense papers. The central positioning relative to demonstration-based IRL and existing alignment methods remains intact. Publication updates to retained references are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: Most scientific prose remains unchanged. v6 adds conclusion subsections, ethics and LLM-use statements and acknowledgments, updates author/affiliation information and citation style, and relabels the existing supplementary sections 6–9 as Appendices C–F.

P2.justification: v6 adds comparison Figure 1 and completely redraws the earlier pipeline as Figure 2. It moves the jailbreak and difficulty-weighting tables into the main text, removes the duplicated product-versus-sum table, and changes front matter, headers and float placement through the conference layout. This substantially revises visual presentation while retaining the empirical plots.

improvement.justification: v6 improves qualification through explicit data-coverage, scaling-cost and reward-bias limitations. The explanatory diagrams and consolidated table placement also improve navigation without changing the evidence. Release conditions are more explicit, but restricted access and the absence of a concrete access link limit the reproducibility benefit. These support a modest overall improvement rather than a substantive scientific advance.
